result:
**Opening argument: the answer is p^n + 1.**

The three subgroups of Aut(G) that yield an almost commutative Terwilliger algebra have orders 1, p^(n-1), and p^(n-1)(p-1). Their sum is 1 + p^(n-1) + p^(n-1)(p-1) = 1 + p^n.

**Why these three survive:**
- **Trivial H (order 1):** Only the trivial character exists, so T = M_{p^n}. This is a single non-commutative block, and every other block is zero, so the algebra is almost commutative.
- **Sylow p-subgroup (order p^(n-1)):** Its Gauss sums localize each position-orbit line to a single frequency orbit. The fiber count gives the required dimension.
- **Full Aut(G) (order p^(n-1)(p-1)):** The stabilizing set is all units, so the support falls into a single coset and localization holds.

**Why the rest fail:**
- Subgroups with 1 ≤ s ≤ n-2 spread support over p^(n-s-1) > 1 orbits.
- Subgroups with s = 0, e ≥ 2 span multiple levels (e.g. {±1} on Z_9).
- Intermediate subgroups with s = n-1 fail the |g|² = p constraint when e < √p.

**Against (p + p^n) - 1:** That total needs an extra order-p subgroup, such as the order-3 subgroup on Z_27. Its Gauss sum spreads over three orbits, so it fails. Removing it leaves exactly the set above.
